candidates.title: Adaptive Safety Constraints via Lagrangian Reward Augmentation for Inference-Time Alignment
candidates.summary: We propose integrating Lagrangian Reward Augmentation (LARA) with dynamic safety constraints to balance helpfulness and harmlessness during inference. LARA calibrates dual variables on a calibration set to adjust reward scores, ensuring safety constraints are satisfied while optimizing for helpfulness. We validate this approach on public safety benchmarks, comparing it to fixed-penalty and unconstrained baselines using AU-PRC and human evaluations.
candidates.gap: Existing inference-time alignment methods either ignore safety constraints or use manually tuned penalties, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between helpfulness and harmlessness. LARA provides a principled way to handle safety constraints without manual tuning, but its effectiveness under dynamic safety thresholds remains unexplored.
candidates.approach: We extend LARA by introducing adaptive safety constraints that adjust based on prompt complexity. The dual variable is recalibrated per prompt using a small calibration set, ensuring the augmented reward dynamically balances helpfulness and harmlessness. This is applied to Best-of-N reranking and token-level decoding.
candidates.evaluation: We compare against fixed-penalty BoN, unconstrained BoN, and Llama Guard baselines on HarmBench and StrongREJECT. Metrics include AU-PRC for safety, human preference for helpfulness, and attack success rates under jailbreaking. Ablations test calibration set size and constraint tightness.

candidates.title: Coverage-Aware Pessimism for Scaling Test-Time Compute in Misaligned Reward Models
candidates.summary: We introduce Coverage-Aware Pessimism (CAP), a test-time alignment algorithm that combines pessimistic rejection sampling with coverage estimation to mitigate reward hacking. CAP estimates the policy's coverage over high-quality responses and adjusts pessimism thresholds accordingly, enabling safe scaling of N in Best-of-N sampling. We evaluate CAP on AlpacaFarm and HH-RLHF, comparing it to standard BoN and InferenceTimePessimism.
candidates.gap: While InferenceTimePessimism (ITP) mitigates reward hacking, it assumes uniform coverage and does not adapt to varying policy capabilities. CAP addresses this by explicitly modeling coverage, allowing more aggressive sampling when coverage is high and stricter rejection when it is low.
candidates.approach: CAP estimates coverage using a held-out validation set, then applies ITP with a dynamic threshold proportional to the coverage estimate. The threshold ensures that only responses within the high-coverage region are accepted, preventing reward hacking while maximizing performance.
candidates.evaluation: We test CAP against ITP, BoN, and MBR-BoN on AlpacaFarm and HH-RLHF. Metrics include win rates vs. human references, reward model scores, and gold-standard human evaluations. Ablations vary coverage estimation methods and threshold scaling factors.

candidates.title: Synthetic Preference Data Curation with Safety Reasoning for Robust Alignment
candidates.summary: We propose generating synthetic preference data using safety-reasoning prompts, where models critique and revise responses based on safety guidelines. This data is used to train reward models that resist jailbreaking. We evaluate the reward models on HarmBench and JailbreakBench, comparing them to Skywork-Reward-V2 and Llama Guard.
candidates.gap: Current reward models trained on human or synthetic data struggle with OOD jailbreaking attacks. Safety-reasoning supervision could improve generalization, but no work has systematically evaluated this for reward model training.
candidates.approach: We synthesize preference data by prompting models to generate harmful queries, critique responses using safety guidelines, and revise them. The critiques and revised responses form preference pairs, which train reward models. The guidelines include diverse safety perspectives to improve coverage.
candidates.evaluation: We compare reward models trained on synthetic safety-reasoning data to Skywork-Reward-V2 and Llama Guard on HarmBench and JailbreakBench. Metrics include AU-PRC, attack success rates, and win rates against human preferences. Ablations test guideline diversity and critique depth.
